Extract title and snippet server-side and store in DB

Compute plain-text title (first text line) and snippet (subsequent text,
skipping images/URLs/code blocks/HRs) at atom create/update time and
persist as columns on the atoms table. This eliminates client-side
extraction, gives a single source of truth, and ensures snippets have
enough content even when the first 1000+ chars are non-text.

feat: add atomic-cloud management plane for managed hosting

Standalone actix-web server (crates/atomic-cloud) that handles the full
lifecycle of managed Atomic instances: Stripe billing, Fly.io VM
orchestration, and a customer dashboard.

Cache global canvas payload with debounced rebuild

The /api/canvas/global endpoint recomputes PCA, metadata, edges, and
clustering on every request. At high atom counts this is expensive
(embedding blob scan + power iteration + edge load + label propagation).

Changes:

- Rewrite get_canvas_atom_metadata_light to a single LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY
  in both SQLite and Postgres, replacing two correlated subqueries per
  row. primary_tag is now MIN(name) (deterministic) instead of an
  unordered LIMIT 1.

- Introduce CanvasCache on AtomicCore, holding Arc<GlobalCanvasData>
  behind an RwLock with a generation counter and an optional rebuilder
  closure registered at construction. compute_and_get_canvas_data now
  returns Arc<GlobalCanvasData>, reads the cache on entry and populates
  on miss.

- Two invalidation flavors:
  * invalidate() — eager clear for direct user mutations (atom/tag CRUD,
    rebuild_semantic_edges, reembed_all_atoms, recreate_vector_index).
  * invalidate_debounced() — keeps stale payload visible and spawns a
    background rebuild after 500ms via spawn_blocking; only the latest
    request wins via the gen counter so batch event storms collapse
    into one rebuild. Used by wrap_event_for_cache on EmbeddingComplete
    and TaggingComplete, and by the per-batch edge pipeline.

- Thread Option<CanvasCache> through process_embedding_batch,
  process_pending_embeddings, and process_pending_edges so each
  completed edge batch can invalidate the cache as edges land. Move
  the edge-pipeline kickoff out of storage::rebuild_semantic_edges_sync
  into the facade so the cache handle can be supplied.

- Warm the cache per-database on atomic-server startup, sequenced via
  spawn_blocking to avoid an N-way PCA spike.

Unify structured LLM output through providers::structured

Adds a single entry point for every typed-JSON LLM call in atomic-core and
migrates all five existing call sites (wiki synthesis, briefing final pass,
tag extraction ×2, tag consolidation, tag merge) off their bespoke retry
and parse loops. The new helper owns the schema portability lint, tolerant
parsing, prompt-based fallback, and retry orchestration that each caller
used to reimplement (inconsistently).

providers::structured (new module):
- call_structured<T>(call) and call_structured_with_provider<T>(call, provider).
  Production uses the former (resolves provider from ProviderConfig);
  tests inject via the latter so the full pipeline is exercisable without
  hitting a real LLM.
- StructuredCall<T> builder with with_params, with_max_retries, with_strict.
- lint_schema() rejects oneOf / anyOf / nullable unions / missing
  additionalProperties:false / optional properties. Runs before any call.
- parse_tolerant<T>() tries raw → code-fence-stripped → outermost {..}
  substring before giving up. Handles ```json fences, prose preambles,
  and trailing "let me know if you need anything else" epilogues.
- Prompt-based fallback: if primary parse fails, fires one more call
  WITHOUT structured_output, appending a "reply with ONLY a single JSON
  object matching this schema" user nudge. Handles weak providers that
  silently ignore response_format.
- StructuredCallError enum with SchemaLint, Provider, ParseFailed, Other;
  ParseFailed carries attempts and a 500-char response preview.
- with_strict(false) escape hatch for models known to reject OpenAI strict
  mode (default stays true — production callers unchanged).

Call-site migrations (~140 lines of duplicated retry/parse loops removed):
- wiki/mod.rs: call_llm_for_wiki_typed becomes a ~25-line wrapper around
  call_structured. Extracted wiki_generation_schema() to a named function
  so it's callable from lint/snapshot tests.
- briefing/agentic.rs: final_briefing_call drops the hand-rolled retry loop.
- extraction.rs: all three call sites (extract_tags_from_content,
  extract_tags_from_chunk, consolidate_atom_tags) share extraction_schema(),
  consolidation_schema(), and extraction_params() helpers. Deleted the
  private parse_tag_extractions and strip_markdown_fences helpers — the
  shared tolerant parser covers both responsibilities.
- extraction.rs: ExtractionResult is now a #[serde(untagged)] enum with
  Wrapped{tags} and Bare(Vec<_>) variants, so the dual-shape tolerance
  (some providers return {"tags":[...]}, others a bare [...]) is now a
  property of the type instead of a hand-written parse ladder.
- compaction.rs: get_merge_suggestions migrated.

Test coverage (49 new tests, 206 total):
- providers::structured has 15 unit tests for the linter, tolerant parser,

Fix overlay stack growth on back-nav and WS reconnect race

Two issues surfaced in code review of the mobile-prep routing work:

1) RouterBridge appended to the overlay stack on every URL change
whose top entry didn't match. Browser back from reader B to reader A
would produce stack=[A, B, A] instead of reverting to index 0. Each
back/forward cycle grew the stack by two entries. Side-effect: the
`overlayNav.index === -1` guard for first-overlay-open behaviors
could misfire inside a long session.

Fix: embed a monotonic `seq` in `history.state` on every navigateTo.
RouterBridge compares the incoming entry's seq against the previous
one to distinguish forward from back. On back, search the stack for
a matching entry and snap the index to it rather than appending. On
forward, step the index forward when the next entry matches (handles
the browser-forward-after-back case). Cold-loaded URLs have no state,
so Bridge injects seq=0 on first run — otherwise later back-nav to
the cold entry would look like "seq became null" and direction
detection would fail.

Collapsed the per-kind append-if-not-top logic into a single
reconcileOverlayNav helper so reader/graph/wiki-reader cases share
the same stack behavior.

2) HttpTransport.wakeUp (visibilitychange / online handler) skipped
only when this.connected === true. If a socket was mid-connect
(readyState === CONNECTING, this.connected === false), a wake signal
would cancel the pending reconnect timer and fire connectWs() again
— overwriting this.ws and orphaning the in-flight socket. If the
orphaned socket eventually opened, it would fire a spurious
onConnectionChange(true) and leak an undisposed WebSocket.

Fix: additionally skip when this.ws.readyState === CONNECTING.

fix(pwa): exclude OAuth/MCP paths from service-worker navigation fallback

The PWA service worker registered a NavigationRoute that rewrites every
top-level navigation to /index.html, with a denylist that only covered
/api/, /health, and /ws. Top-level navigations to /oauth/authorize

the cached index.html took over the URL and the user landed on the
dashboard with the OAuth query params still in the address bar,
instead of the consent page served by atomic-server.

API/WS requests weren't affected because they're not navigations;
only top-level browser redirects (which is exactly what claude.ai does
after discovery) triggered the bug.

Add /oauth/, /.well-known/, and /mcp to navigateFallbackDenylist so the
browser lets those requests reach atomic-server.

feat(editor): Obsidian-style live-preview markdown editor for atoms Adds an in-place markdown editor to the atom reader. Toggling to edit mode now shows an Obsidian-like live preview — headings, links, emphasis, and images render as their view-mode counterparts; clicking into a line unfolds only that line's raw markdown for editing. View and edit share the same scroll container, and the toggle preserves content position (not raw scrollTop) so the user's focus doesn't jump when flipping between modes. ## What's new - Rich CodeMirror 6 extension in `src/lib/codemirror-rich-markdown.ts`: line decorations for h1–h6, paragraph/list/blank-line spacing, inline mark hiding (`##`, `**`, `[...]`, escape backslashes), and full-line image widgets with click-to-edit behaviour. - Shared image-size cache (`src/lib/image-size-cache.ts`) so CM's ImageWidget and view's MarkdownImage agree on heights and don't cause toggle-time pop-in. - Scroll-position preservation across view↔edit (captures topmost visible block + its y-offset, restores after mode flip). - Dark-mode selection and Ctrl+F search-panel theming that actually beats CM's deep-specificity default rules. - Extensive Playwright-based regression harness at `scripts/harness/` (`npm run editor-harness`), plus a dozen targeted `check-*.mjs` scripts each protecting against a specific class of bug. - `src/lib/EDITOR.md` — a detailed guide to the non-obvious parts of this area so the same lessons don't get re-learned next time. ## Key technical decisions - **Virtualisation disabled via `patches/@codemirror+view+6.38.8.patch`.** CM's heightmap relies on lazily-measured "estimated" heights for off-viewport lines. Our decorations produce ~20× height variance (h1 = 40px, image widget = 400px+), which makes the heightmap drift every time a new line scrolls in — visibly reflowing the content and breaking click-to-position mapping. Patching `VP.Margin` to `10_000_000` makes CM render the whole document up front. Measurements: 22ms mount on 14KB atoms, 150ms on 450KB Wikipedia atoms. Beyond ~5000 lines this becomes noticeable; the escalation path is segment-based rendering, not more heightmap tuning. - **Two-layer decoration system.** A ViewPlugin handles everything that can be expressed as inline decorations; a StateField handles whole-line image widgets because block decorations aren't allowed from a ViewPlugin. The StateField matches the line text directly against regexes for bare (`![alt](url)`) and linked (`[![alt](url)](link)`) image patterns — the latter is what web clippers emit for every Wikipedia figure. - **`activeLines` is caret-only.** Range selections don't activate lines they traverse; otherwise drag-selecting across a paragraph containing blank lines would un-collapse each blank (growing from 0 → 28px) and shove everything below the cursor down by a line-height per blank in the selection. Fixed after users saw "selection is adding padding between blocks" and the harness confirmed up to 220px of mid-drag layout drift. - **Prose-matching line margins.** `cm-md-p-start/-end` at 1.25em match Tailwind Typography's `

` collapsed gap exactly. `cm-md-imgp-start/-end` were originally 2em — double the effective view-mode gap, compounding into 128px of drift over 8 images. Halved to 1.25em after measuring view's actual `

→ wrapper → img` collapse stack. - **Blank line collapsing.** `.cm-md-blank { height: 0; line-height: 0 }` plus `.cm-md-blank > br { display: none }` — the `
` removal is load-bearing; without it the empty block doesn't qualify for CSS margin-collapse and paragraph gaps get double-counted. ## Bugs we had to pay for Several of these were paid for with full diagnostic scripts that remain in `scripts/harness/` as regression guards: - **Image click dispatch race.** The decoration swap (inline-replace → block widget) detaches the IMG element mid-gesture. Every naïve handling strategy failed differently: `click` doesn't fire (target detached), `mouseup` fires outside cm-content, `mousedown` + return false lets CM re-dispatch against the rebuilt layout, `mousedown` + preventDefault + return true wins the click but leaves the heightmap stale. `mouseSelectionStyle` returning a custom style somehow wedges CM's internal mouse state. Resolution: synchronous dispatch from mousedown + preventDefault + return true, plus a one-shot `mousedown` capture listener armed right after the image click that resolves the VERY NEXT click via `document.caretRangeFromPoint` + CM's `posFromDOM` (bypassing the stale heightmap for the duration of its sync gap). - **Link-expansion selection flash.** Clicking a paragraph containing a hidden link landed mousedown at doc-pos A (against the collapsed visible text); CM flipped the line to active, the link syntax revealed, text shifted, mouseup at the same screen coord landed at doc-pos B, and CM selected A..B. A `clickCollapseHandler` collapses range selections where the pointer moved ≤4px (modifier-key clicks untouched). - **CM's `&light.cm-focused > .cm-scroller > .cm-selectionLayer .cm-selectionBackground` out-specific'd any `.cm-selectionBackground` rule in our theme** — accent purple only landed while the editor was unfocused. Fixed by matching selector depth in `src/index.css`. Same trick for the Ctrl+F search panel. - **Wikipedia URLs with escaped parens** (`...\(cropped\).jpg`) broke the image-widget regex at the first `)`. `URL_CHARS` now accepts `(?:\\.|[^)\s])+` to include escape sequences. - **Harness `measureByText` stripped nothing**, so `"25.04.0"` in view never matched the `"### 25\.04\.0"` raw cm-line in edit and tests saw phantom drift. Now normalises escapes, link syntax, and emphasis markers. - **`posAtCoords` staleness** is documented but unresolved at the CM level — our one-shot listener closes the real-world window. ## What was tried and rejected - **Pre-mounting edit mode in the background** (to make click-Edit feel instant on huge atoms). Two attempts: - `visibility: hidden` + `position: absolute`: 6/10 harness, +192px toggle drift (image widgets measure against wrong container width, image-size cache populates in wrong order). - `display: none`: 5/10 harness, catastrophic ~8500px scroll- stability drift (CM's heightmap never initialises without layout). - Kept as mount-on-click. 150ms on 450KB atoms is the current ceiling. - **Grid-overlay pre-mount** got total heights identical but per-line positions still drifted up to 216px. Documented in `EDITOR.md`. ## Harness New: `npm run editor-harness`. Ten scenarios (scroll stability, click accuracy, toggle roundtrip, image-cutoff preservation, rapid- toggle stability, image-click reveal, heading-mark fade, height parity, scroll-no-shift, heading↔paragraph boundary clicks). Baseline: 8/10 on the kdenlive state-of-the-year fixture — the two failures are sub-perceptible (4px click edge miss, 28px toggle drift on one landmark). fix(editor): preserve user-typed blank lines + make list exit actually exit

Two bugs from the new-atom authoring flow:

1. **Consecutive blank lines invisible.** Every blank line got the
   `cm-md-blank` 0-height class, so typing Enter twice looked identical
   to typing Enter once — the user couldn't add real vertical space.
   Fix: only collapse the LAST blank in any run. Earlier blanks stay
   full height, giving the user N-1 lines of visual breathing room
   per N typed Enters, while still letting the adjacent paragraph
   margins collapse through the final blank as before.

2. **List exit doesn't really exit.** After typing `- item`, Enter,
   Enter to exit, then typing "hello", the text came out styled and
   parsed as a list item continuation. Root cause: `@codemirror/lang-
   markdown`'s `insertNewlineContinueMarkup` removes the bullet marker
   but leaves the cursor on a zero-width empty line at the end of the
   doc — so the next typed character lands immediately after the
   previous list item's `\n`, with no blank-line separator. Markdown
   treats that as a lazy continuation, and our `cm-md-li` decoration
   (plus the parser) faithfully paint it as a list item.

   Fix: high-precedence Enter handler that runs before lang-markdown's
   default. When the cursor is at the end of a marker-only line inside
   a ListItem, we replace the marker-only line with an actual newline,
   so a real blank line sits between the list and whatever the user
   types next. Markdown can't turn the follow-up text into a lazy
   continuation.

3. (**Bonus**) Tightened the line-range math in the ListItem /
   BulletList / Paragraph decoration handlers: CM markdown nodes
   often carry a `to` value at the *start of the next line* (i.e. just
   past the trailing `\n`), so `doc.lineAt(node.to)` returned the line
   AFTER the node and our decorations leaked onto it. Added a
   `lastLineOf(doc, node)` helper that walks back one char first.
   Belt-and-braces for the list-exit case; also quietly prevents other
   rare leaks.

fix(editor): restore click-to-move-cursor and click-drag selection

User-reported: in edit mode, clicking into a typed sentence didn't move
the cursor; click-and-drag didn't select text; flashes of wrong
selections would briefly appear and then correct.

Root cause was the same for all three symptoms: CM's heightmap
measures each `.cm-line` via `getBoundingClientRect`, which includes
padding but NOT margin. All our `.cm-line.cm-md-*` decorations used
`margin-top/bottom` for vertical spacing between blocks. Over a long
document with many spaced lines (headings, paragraphs, 50+ list
items), the accumulated invisible-to-heightmap margin threw off
`posAtCoords` — clicks far into the doc resolved to wrong positions.

Fix: convert every `.cm-line.cm-md-*` spacing rule from `margin-*` to
`padding-top`. Single-sided (bottom-less) padding preserves the same
effective gap as margin-collapse in view mode — the NEXT block's
`padding-top` supplies the gap, so consecutive paragraphs get exactly
1.25em between them rather than doubling to 2.5em. Padding is INSIDE
the line box, so CM's heightmap tracks it accurately and all clicks
route to the intended doc position.

Also added a lightweight mouse-gesture freeze (module-level boolean
flipped by capture-phase DOM listeners, no state dispatch inside
mousedown so CM's drag state-machine isn't disturbed). It suppresses
decoration rebuilds between `mousedown` and `mouseup`, which
eliminates the brief "flash a range selection then collapse it"
symptom when clicking paragraphs with hidden link syntax.

Regression envelope: full harness 7/10 vs 8/10 baseline — the one
regression is ~16px of extra view↔edit toggle drift because padding
doesn't *perfectly* mirror margin-collapse behaviour. No impact on
click accuracy or cursor movement, which is the fix's actual goal.

New harness guards locked in:
  - check-fresh-typing.mjs: type a sentence, click inside it, verify
    cursor moves to the clicked word.
  - check-drag-select.mjs: press-and-drag produces a range selection.
  - check-click-no-flash.mjs: single-click in a link-bearing paragraph
    never produces a transient range.

fix: prevent duplicate embedding runs from pipeline scheduler

Two bugs caused atoms to be embedded twice on every scheduler tick:

1. pipeline_task.rs called both process_pending_embeddings_due and
   process_pending_tagging_due in the same tick. Both functions call
   enqueue_pipeline_jobs_from_statuses_sync followed by
   process_queued_pipeline_jobs. The second call's ON CONFLICT reset
   jobs already claimed by the first call back to state='pending',
   causing them to be claimed and processed a second time.

   process_pending_embeddings_due already covers atoms with
   (embedding_status='complete' AND tagging_status='pending'), so
   process_pending_tagging_due was purely redundant.

2. enqueue_pipeline_jobs_from_statuses_sync used ON CONFLICT ... DO
   UPDATE SET state='pending', lease_until=NULL unconditionally. Any
   concurrent or racing enqueue call could interrupt an actively-leased
   processing job, regardless of cause.

Fixes:
- Remove the redundant process_pending_tagging_due call from the
  scheduler tick
- Preserve state='processing' and lease_until in the ON CONFLICT
  clause when the existing job has an active (non-expired) lease

fix(canvas): harden LocalGraphView against WebGL context exhaustion

LocalGraphView blew up the route-level Error Boundary with

    TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'blendFunc')
        at new Sigma (...)

whenever Sigma's constructor called gl.blendFunc(...) on a null WebGL
context. The root cause is the browser's per-tab WebGL context cap
(~16 on Chrome, ~8 on Safari): sigma.kill() detaches the canvas but the
underlying GL context lingers until GC, so rapid re-centers of the local
graph (combined with the always-mounted main SigmaCanvas) eventually
exhaust the pool. The next `new Sigma` then receives a canvas whose
getContext returns null and crashes on the first GL state call.

Two changes:

1. Introduce a releaseSigma() helper that calls sigma.kill() and then
   explicitly invokes WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext() on every canvas
   inside the container. That frees the GL slot immediately rather than
   waiting on GC. Use it from both the in-effect "previous sigma" cleanup
   and the effect's return cleanup.
2. Wrap `new Sigma(...)` in try/catch. If the context can't be acquired
   we surface a friendly error state instead of letting the crash hit
   the Error Boundary and blank the whole page.

This is the load-bearing prerequisite for the Reports primitive

existing atoms migrate to kind='captured' and no production code

Schema (SQLite V17→V18, Postgres 014_atoms_kind.sql):
  atoms.kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'captured'
  CREATE INDEX idx_atoms_kind ON atoms(kind)

Types:

first writer in phase 2; the existing scheduler tick and legacy system
tasks (DailyBriefing / DraftPipeline / GraphMaintenance) are intentionally
left on their current interval-based path, per the plan doc.

What's in:

- SQLite V19 + Postgres migration 015 creating `task_runs` (id, task_id,
  subject_id, state, trigger, attempts/max_attempts, lease_until,
  next_attempt_at, scope JSON, result_id, last_error, timestamps).
- Models: `TaskRunState` (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Abandoned) and
  `TaskRunTrigger` (Schedule/Manual) as real Rust enums with snake_case
  serde; `TaskRun` struct as the storage-boundary owned form.
- `TaskRunStore` trait + SQLite and Postgres implementations. Every state
  transition is a conditional UPDATE with a `state` predicate so a stale
  reclaimer can't double-complete a row that already moved on; storage
  returns `bool` so callers detect lost races without re-reading.
- `scheduler::ledger` module composing those primitives:
  - `claim_or_create` finds-or-inserts a runnable row and attempts the
    conditional claim; on success returns a `RunHandle`.
  - `RunHandle` spawns a 5-min heartbeat task that conditionally refreshes
    the 15-min lease; `complete` / `fail` are the terminal writers. Drop
    aborts only the heartbeat — a panicked run leaves a `running` row
    whose lease eventually expires and gets reclaimed by the next tick,
    which is the correct crash-recovery behavior.
  - `backoff(attempts)` = `base * 2^(n-1) * rand(0.5, 1.5)` capped at 1h.
- 17 tests: state-machine round-trips, claim-wins-exactly-once under
  16-way contention (run 50x without flakes), live-lease blocks
  re-claim, expired-lease reclaim leaves `attempts` untouched (process
  crash ≠ logic failure), heartbeat extends only when running, terminal
  completes/fails are no-ops on already-terminal rows, retry-vs-abandon
  branching, find_runnable orders by earliest next_attempt_at and
  skips future-pending and terminal rows, backoff jitter and cap bounds.
- Uuid v7 for run IDs so history queries get bonus time-locality.

`uuid` gains the v7 feature; otherwise no new deps.

'report') with structured provenance and per-citation excerpts. The
briefing keeps working as-is; phase 3 will collapse it onto this

so this is the ledger's first real production caller.

- `reports`: definition row with research_prompt, source/context scope
  (tag ids, window, kinds), citation_policy, schedule (cron expr +
  IANA tz), max_*, enabled, output_atom_tags, advisory cache columns.
- `report_findings`: durable provenance from a finding atom back to its
  report definition. Survives report deletion (ON DELETE SET NULL) and
  run-row GC (no FK on run_id).
- `report_finding_citations`: (finding_atom_id, cited_atom_id, position,
  excerpt) so "which findings cite atom X" is a single index lookup.

Module shape

- `crate::models::Report` + four typed enums (SourceScopeWindow,
  ContextScopeMode, ContextScopeWindow, CitationPolicy) plus
  CreateReportRequest / UpdateReportRequest with serde defaults that
  match production seeding ("captured" kinds, source_only policy,
  enabled = true).
- `crate::reports::scope`: resolves source atoms from (tag subtree +
  window + kinds + cap) and builds the agent's ContextFilter
  (excludes source ids and prior findings from this same report).
- `crate::reports::schedule`: cron parser via the `cron` crate +
  chrono-tz. Invalid schedules log and report not-due so a malformed
  row can't wedge the scheduler.
- `crate::reports::agentic`: generalized agent loop. System prompt
  scaffold composed with the report's research_prompt. Semantic_search
  is parameterized by the context filter and post-filtered by tag
  scope (precomputed once per run), time window, kinds, and the
  excluded-id set. Run-scoped citable-evidence map: source atoms
  numbered [1]..[N] up front; under source_and_context, context
  results get next numbers on first appearance and the marker is
  surfaced to the agent.
- `crate::reports::runner::run_report`: full lifecycle. Claims via
  `ledger::claim_or_create`. Empty scope terminates with
  RunOutcome::EmptyScope (no atom written, no LLM call). On success
  the atom + provenance + every citation row commit in a single
  `write_finding_transactionally` storage call so a partial write
  cannot orphan a finding atom.

REST surface (atomic-server)

- GET/POST /api/reports
- GET/PUT/DELETE /api/reports/:id
- PATCH /api/reports/:id/enabled
- POST /api/reports/:id/run (202 + run id; finding queryable via the

- GET /api/reports/:id/findings

Background loop in main.rs runs every 60s, iterates DBs × enabled
reports, and dispatches due ones through ledger::claim_or_create. Each

- `AtomStore`: `list_atoms_for_report_scope` + `count_atoms_for_report_scope`

  Postgres so the runner doesn't reimplement subtree expansion.
- `ReportStore`: CRUD + the transactional finding writer + history

reports phase 3: review fixes (watermark, citations, resume, events)

Five fixes from review on the phase-3 collapse commit. One real
correctness bug (P1), four robustness/UX gaps (P2). +1 net LOC of
production code; the rest is tests and inline rationale.

P1 — advance report watermark from run start, not completion
    (runner.rs)

The previous shape stamped `last_run_at = Utc::now()` after the LLM
returned. For `source_scope_window = SinceLastRun`, any atom captured
between scope resolution and run finish would have `created_at` inside
the just-crossed gap and never get picked up on the next tick. Now
snapshot the resolution-time watermark at the top of `execute()` and
thread it through both `RunInner` branches; the finding atom's own
`created_at` continues to record the completion time (distinct concern).
Regression test asserts the stamped watermark falls inside
`[before_run, after_run]` rather than after both.

P2 — store the actual [N] marker number as citation position
    (agentic.rs)

`extract_citations` was incrementing a per-appearance counter and
writing that as `position`. The dashboard renders `[N]` markers in
finding prose and looks up citations by N, so out-of-order or repeated
markers (`[3]` before `[1]`, or `[1]` twice) made the popovers point at
the wrong source or fail to resolve at all. Now store N itself and
dedupe repeated markers — repeated `[1]`s render multiple popovers
backed by a single row, which is also what the composite PK
`(finding_atom_id, cited_atom_id, position)` requires.

The existing `maps_marker_to_known_atom` test asserted the old
appearance-counter behavior; updated to expect deduped rows with marker
numbers, plus a new
`extract_citations_out_of_sequence_preserves_marker_number` test that
nails the regression directly.

P2 — broadcast atom-created after a successful report run
    (atomic-server::main.rs, routes/reports.rs)

The reports loop calls `run_report` directly and writes the finding
atom through storage, bypassing the event bridge. The dashboard widget
listens for `atom-created` filtered by `kind === 'report'`; without an
emission it would only show new findings after a manual refresh. Both
the scheduled loop and the manual `POST /api/reports/:id/run` handler
now broadcast `ServerEvent::AtomCreated` on the `Succeeded` outcome
(fetching the freshly-written atom via `get_atom`). Failures on either
the run or the broadcast lookup log but never abort the calling task.

P2 — fix atom-created payload shape in BriefingWidget
    (BriefingWidget.tsx)

`AtomWithTags` uses `#[serde(flatten)]` for its inner `atom`, and the
event-normalizer delivers the whole AtomWithTags as the payload — so
the atom's fields (including `kind`) live at the top of the payload,
not under `.atom`. The previous `payload.atom?.kind` was always
undefined, so the widget never refreshed on a new finding. One-line
fix: `payload.kind`.

P2 — make briefings → findings migration resumable
    (reports/seed.rs)

The previous loop generated fresh UUIDs per row, so a crash between
any per-row commit and the final flag flip would, on restart, write the
same legacy briefings into a second set of finding atoms. The migration
now derives a stable atom id (`legacy-briefing-{briefing.id}`) and
gates each write on `get_atom` not seeing that id already; resumed runs
skip already-migrated rows and log a `resumed_skip` count. The
`legacy-briefing-` prefix protects against the (vanishing) chance of
collision with a user-authored captured atom whose id happens to match
a legacy briefing's. New
`migrate_briefings_to_findings_resumes_after_partial_crash` test
pre-stamps one row's target atom as if a prior boot had crashed and
asserts the second run migrates only the remaining row.

reports phase 4b: review fixes (enum wire format, finding tuple decode)

Two P-bugs caught in review.

P1 — TS enum wire shapes didn't match Rust serde derives:

- SourceScopeWindow is `#[serde(rename_all="snake_case")]` over
  `{SinceLastRun, Duration(String)}`, which externally-tagged
  serializes as either the bare string `"since_last_run"` or the
  object `{"duration": "P7D"}`. The TS shipped `{kind: ...}` /
  `{kind: 'iso_duration', value: ...}`, which the server rejects at
  deserialization. Every "New Report" save was failing on the default
  source-scope window.
- ContextScopeMode variants are `same_as_source | all | explicit`.
  The TS had `tags` and `none` — neither exists server-side. The
  "Custom tags" radio mapped to a nonexistent variant; "No context"
  had no backend home at all (the substitute is `explicit` with an
  empty tag list, which is now what the editor emits).
- CitationPolicy variants are `source_only | source_and_context`.
  The TS had `context_citable`. Switching policy always failed save.
- ContextScopeWindow is a separate enum with `OlderThanSource`
  instead of `SinceLastRun`; was aliased to SourceScopeWindow.

ScopeField now accepts the union of both wire shapes and degrades
unknown variants (e.g. `older_than_source`) to "all time" rather than
crashing — the variant has no picker option to create it in v1.

P2 — `list_findings_for_report` returns `Vec<(ReportFinding,
AtomWithTags)>`, which serializes as JSON `[[finding, atom], ...]`,
not `[{finding, atom}, ...]`. The reports store was caching the raw
tuple, so `lastFinding.atom.content` was reading the `atom` property
off a tuple object (undefined) — the reports view crashed as soon as
any listed report had at least one finding. The store now
destructures `[finding, atom]` at the cache boundary.

The existing featuredReport store works around the same wire shape
by tuple-destructuring in its callback; reports now follows the
same pattern.

reports: review fixes (subscription scope, failure detection, seed flag, cron normalize, schema version)

Five findings from external review, all real bugs.

P2 — Subscription tied to list loading (src/stores/reports.ts):

  The atom-created subscription was set up inside fetchAll and torn
  down inside reset(). Deep-linking to /reports/:id bypassed fetchAll
  entirely; opening the detail view from the list unmounted the list
  and tore down the subscription. Either way Run Now from the detail
  view never observed completion until the 5-minute stale guard.

  Subscription is now session-scoped infrastructure: a dedicated
  ensureSubscription() action (idempotent, guarded by hasSubscription).
  Both ReportsFullView and ReportDetailView call it on mount. reset()
  no longer touches the subscription — caches reset, infrastructure
  survives.

P2 — Failure detection relied on last_run_at (ReportDetailView.tsx):

  The runner intentionally does NOT update last_run_at on failure
  (first-run failures would otherwise stamp an unparseable value into
  the schedule anchor and silently wedge the report). The detail
  view's poll compared `last_run_at >= dispatchedAt` to identify our
  dispatch's failure, so first-run failures and failures after a
  prior success never resolved until the 5-minute stale guard.

  Snapshot last_error at dispatch time; poll detects a new failure
  when current last_error differs (especially: null → set). Edge
  case where a concurrent scheduled tick fails at the same time is
  indistinguishable from our own failure — the user gets a failure
  toast either way, which is the right UX.

P2 — Seeding didn't respect a cleared featured pointer (seed.rs):

  Idempotency was anchored on `dashboard.featured_report_id`
  pointing at an extant report. Clearing the pointer (legitimate
  user action) or deleting the seeded report caused the next boot
  to silently re-seed and re-feature.

  Introduced `reports.default_briefing_seeded` as the one-shot flag.
  Set after the first successful seed; subsequent boots see it and
  exit immediately. Pre-flag DBs (where only the featured pointer
  signals "seeded") get a one-time migration on first boot: detect
  the pointer + report, set the flag, return without re-seeding.

  Three new tests:
  - seed_does_not_recreate_after_user_clears_featured_pointer
  - seed_does_not_recreate_after_user_deletes_seeded_report
  - seed_migrates_pre_flag_dbs_without_reseeding

P2 — Five-field cron rejected at server boundary (ScheduleField.tsx):

  The editor's "Custom cron" input accepted both 5- and 6-field
  expressions and previewed both as valid. The backend's `cron`
  crate requires 6 fields. Users entering `0 9 * * *` saw it as
  valid and only got a 400 on save.

  Normalize 5-field input to 6-field at emit time (prepend `0 `).
  The user's typed text stays unchanged in the input; the
  always-visible canonical cron beneath the picker shows the
  6-field form, doubling as a "here's what we'll save" hint.

P3 — Migration 018 never recorded schema_version (postgres):

  The marker migration ran `SELECT 1` but never inserted into
  schema_version, so the runner's `MAX(version)` query kept
  returning 17 and the no-op re-executed on every startup. Added
  the `INSERT INTO schema_version (version) VALUES (18)` row.

reports: fix FindingReader infinite loading loop

When a finding was opened from the ReportDetailView, FindingReader
got stuck rendering the loading skeleton forever. No errors, just
perpetual loading.

Root cause: classic React effect loop.

  1. cachedFinding selector resolves to the entry in findingsByReport
     populated by the ReportDetailView when it fetched the list.
  2. FindingReader's load effect ran with cachedFinding in deps.
     Called fetchFinding(atomId).
  3. fetchFinding writes back into findingsByReport on every call —
     the `existing.map(...)` update-in-place returns a new array with
     a new object at the matching position, even when nothing actually
     changed.
  4. The cachedFinding selector re-emitted with a fresh reference.
  5. Effect deps changed → effect re-ran → goto 2.

The loop fired the fetch over and over; `isLoading` flipped
true/false at every cycle, so the user saw the loading skeleton
permanently.

Two fixes:

- FindingReader's effect drops cachedFinding from its dep array and
  reads the cache once via useReportsStore.getState() inside the
  effect. The cache lookup still seeds `loaded` synchronously so a
  pre-fetch render isn't a blank skeleton, but cache changes no
  longer retrigger the fetch. Effect only re-runs on atomId change.
- fetchFinding's cache merge gates on actual change. If the cached
  row already matches (same atom updated_at + finding run_id + name
  snapshot), the set() is skipped entirely. Downstream subscribers
  (TabStrip, other selectors over findingsByReport) no longer
  re-emit on a no-op refresh.

postgres: widen atom_positions to f64 + Obsidian import on PG

Two PG-vs-SQLite gaps shaken out by the slice 3-8 e2e suite.

atom_positions.x / y were declared `REAL` (32-bit single) but the Rust
model is `f64`. sqlx's strict decoding refuses to widen REAL into f64,
so the GET path returned a 500 and the PUT path silently rounded
writes. SQLite was unaffected (its REAL is always 8 bytes), which is
why the bug hid until canvas-positions hit Postgres in the e2e run.

Fix: migration 020_atom_positions_double.sql widens both columns to
DOUBLE PRECISION (existing rows up-cast cleanly), and the v1 schema is
patched at the source so fresh installs land at the post-020 column
type. Other f64 decode sites were audited — semantic_edges and
search-relevance scores use f32 against REAL columns and match.

Obsidian import previously dropped into a raw SQLite connection for
the hierarchical-folder-tag path (`as_sqlite().ok_or_else(...)`),
returning a 400 Configuration error on Postgres. The hierarchical
walk needs parent-ID semantics, which the existing `get_or_create_tag`
trait method (parent-name-based) can't express.

Added two new storage primitives that both backends implement:
- get_or_create_tag_with_parent_id(name, parent_id) → (id, created)
  — returns whether the row was freshly inserted so the importer
  keeps an accurate tags_created stat. PG races via ON CONFLICT on
  the existing (db_id, LOWER(name), COALESCE(parent_id, '')) unique
  index and uses created_at-equality to detect winner. SQLite falls
  back to a name-only lookup before INSERT to handle its global
  UNIQUE(name COLLATE NOCASE) constraint cleanly.
- link_tags_to_atom_with_source(atom_id, tag_ids, source) — INSERT
  ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with an explicit source label so the
  importer can mark folder/frontmatter tags as 'manual' (the auto-
  tagger uses 'auto' through the existing link_tags_to_atom path).

`AtomicCore::import_obsidian_vault` was refactored to drive both
paths through the new primitives, and the local `get_or_create_tag`
helper + the SQLite escape hatch are gone. The e2e test now asserts
success on both backends and exercises the parent-id chain with a
nested `Topics/Science/` vault layout.

postgres: propagate schema_version read errors instead of re-running migrations

run_migrations_inner decoded MAX(version) as i64 against an INTEGER (int4)
column; sqlx's strict type check rejected the decode and the error was
swallowed by unwrap_or(0), so every open of an already-migrated database
treated it as fresh and re-ran all migrations from 1. IF NOT EXISTS guards
masked this (while appending duplicate schema_version rows on every open)
until a migration referenced a column the legacy table predated, at which
point initialization failed outright.

Decode as i32 to match the column type and propagate both the
table-existence check and the version read as errors — defaulting either
to "fresh database" is never safe. Regression test asserts a second
initialize() appends no schema_version rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

postgres: pin migration advisory lock to a detached connection

pg_advisory_lock is session-level, but run_migrations issued the lock and
unlock through the pool — they can land on different sessions, so the
unlock silently returns false and the lock stays held by an idle pooled
connection, deadlocking every subsequent initialize() on the same pool.
Nothing hit this until code called initialize() twice on one pool, which
the cloud migration orchestrator will do as a matter of course.

Take the lock on a connection detached from the pool: lock and unlock are
guaranteed the same session, and if the future is cancelled mid-migration
the owned connection drops, closing its session and releasing the lock,
instead of returning a lock-holding connection to the pool. Migration
statements keep running through the pool — the lock serializes callers,
the statements don't need its session. (Pinning the statements to the
locked connection or using a pg_advisory_xact_lock transaction both trip
rustc's 'implementation of Send is not general enough' limitation via
sqlx::raw_sql with a borrowed executor under async_trait.)

Verified against a stale schema-version-7 test database: initialize()
upgrades it incrementally to 20 and a second initialize() is a no-op.

scheduler: task_runs retention GC (phase 5)

task_runs is append-per-invocation, so the durable-task-runs work needs
a bound: TaskRunsGcTask (scheduler::gc) runs hourly through the same
runner dispatch as every other system task — dogfooding the ledger, so
GC gets its own bounded run history, and its in-flight row is `running`
(non-terminal) so it can never collect the row recording it.

Policy, evaluated in one SQL statement per backend
(TaskRunStore::gc_task_runs; the Postgres twin fences every scan on
db_id):

- non-terminal rows are never deleted — live execution state
- keep the most recent 50 terminal rows per (task_id, subject_id)
- hard age cap: terminal rows older than 30 days are eligible even
  inside the keep window
- exception: the most recent terminal failure per group survives both
  rules up to 90 days — "why did this feed stop syncing?" must stay
  answerable after success noise ages out

Deletes run oldest-first in bounded batches (500/batch) with a yield
between batches so a desktop user editing atoms isn't stuck behind a
backlog drain on SQLite's single writer. Knobs follow the task.{id}.*
settings convention (task.task_runs_gc.{enabled,interval_minutes,
keep_per_subject,retain_days,retain_failed_days}), read per-DB via
core.storage() at run time with the plan defaults as fallbacks — no
migration seed rows, preserving the empty-settings invariant. Zero,
negative, and unparseable overrides fall back per-knob instead of
becoming "delete history as it lands".

Tests: each policy rule pinned individually at the storage layer
against both backends (tests/storage_tests.rs), plus the task layer in
lib.rs — policy load defaults/overrides, bounded batching via
gc::sweep, dispatch-through-ledger with last_run advance and interval
gating, and the enabled=false gate.

postgres: scope settings by db_id with an explicit '_global' tier

Postgres has no registry.db, so one settings table served both roles
SQLite separates physically: registry-role config (provider, models)
and per-DB state (task.{id}.* scheduler fast-path keys, seed flags).
With no db_id column, per-DB keys collided across logical databases —
the worst-severity follow-up from the task-runs review and load-bearing
for Atomic Cloud's multi-KB tenant databases.

Migration 021 adds `db_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '_global'` and replaces
the PK with (db_id, key). Existing rows land in '_global' — correct for
the provider/model config they overwhelmingly are. Previously-collided
per-DB keys (task.{id}.last_run, GC knobs, reports seed flags, graph-
maintenance watermarks) become orphaned global rows: scoped reads no
longer see them, so that state resets benignly (tasks re-run on the
next tick, the briefing seed re-checks) instead of staying shared.

SettingsStore grows a global tier — get/set/delete_global_setting(s) —
with defaults that delegate to the scoped methods (correct on SQLite,
where file-per-DB does the scoping physically). PostgresStorage scopes
the four existing methods to self.db_id and overrides the global ones
to target the '_global' sentinel (one constant in storage/postgres).

Global (registry-role; switched to the global accessors):

The periodic safety-net job from the plan's "Failure recovery & the
reaper" section, as a directly-testable library pass (reaper.rs:

   idempotent provision_account first; only a failed resume rolls back.
   Rollback hard-deletes the accounts row (no 'failed' tombstone; loud
   error log with the email is the operator's trace) BEFORE dropping
   the tenant database -- the status-guarded DELETE is the atomic claim
   that stops a concurrently resumed signup from re-activating an
   account whose data is being destroyed; the inverted crash window is
   exactly the orphan predicate, healed next pass. Resume attempts are
   capped per pass; surplus rows defer without wedging the loop.
2. Orphaned acct_* databases (no accounts row, no account_databases
   row): reclaimed under the advisory lock derived from the account id
   embedded in the database name (tenant_db_account_id, new inverse of
   tenant_db_name), with the row-absence proof re-checked under the
   lock immediately before the drop.

   slice-1 crashed-deletion follow-up): cleared once older than a
   settle grace. Migration 003 adds subdomains_reserved.created_at
   (additive) so residue is distinguishable from a deletion in flight
   between its reserve and row-delete steps; delete_account re-ups the
   column on conflict to keep retried deletions shielded.
4. Hygiene: purge magic links expired >24h, expired sessions, lapsed
   reservations.

keyed on a hash of the account id -- contention skips, observably in

the connection. Live signups/deletions take no reaper locks; safety

cloud: deploy gating — boot fleet migration, readiness, operator surface

Slice 5, phase 2 (plan: "Schema migration on deploy" steps 1-5 + the
failure-rate policy table + "Multi-pod boot" + "Rollback").

- Migration 009 (additive): deploy_runs — one row per pod boot
  (target_version, started/finished, total/migrated/failed,
  deploy_status, advanced_at), giving operators per-boot history and
  the awaiting-review acknowledgment a durable, fleet-visible home.
- FleetMigrator (fleet_migration.rs): enumerate lagging active tenants,
  fan out under a concurrency cap (default 16), per tenant connect a
  bounded single-connection PostgresStorage and run initialize() —
  atomic-core's advisory-locked runner IS the multi-pod story (racing
  pods serialize per tenant; the loser no-ops and re-records the same
  success; racing is safe, merely wasteful — single-pod-claims-the-run
  stays deferred per plan). Failures record migration_failed_at +
  bounded error + exponential retry_after backoff for the reaper and
  never abort the run; the wall clock abandons in-flight work honestly
  (timed_out; unattempted tenants stay enumerated for the next run).
- deploy.rs: the policy (<1% ready — stragglers ride the CloudAuth 503
  + reaper retries; 1-10% awaiting_review; ≥10% rollback_required;
  over-limit migration_timeout; thresholds and wall clock are serve
  flags), deploy_runs persistence, and the Readiness state machine:
  serve boots in migrating mode, the NEW public /ready (joining
  /health, which stays up throughout) answers 503 until the gate's
  verdict admits, and flips are logged loudly with every policy input.
  awaiting_review holds re-check their run row on each probe, so a
  control-plane `deploy advance` flips every pod with no push channel.
- Operator surface: `deploy status` (latest run, counts, failure rate,
  every currently-failed tenant migration) and `deploy advance` (flips
  all awaiting_review runs at the latest target version to 'advanced',
  recorded in the control plane so all pods observe it).
  rollback_required deliberately has NO override: a ≥10% rate means
  the migration itself is broken — redeploy the old binary (safe under
  additive-only migrations) and fix it; an override flag would be a
  footgun pointed at the largest blast radius.
- Dispatcher hold: the tick's pause lookup grows a second per-tenant
  hold in the same round trip — active mapping rows lagging the
  compiled target are skipped wholesale (work waits in the ledgers,
  hints untouched), the same predicate CloudAuth's straggler gate
  reads per request.

migrated end to end with the readiness flip and an honest tenant-schema

cloud: failed-migrations reaper arm + additive-only migration lint

Slice 5, phase 3 — the two deliverables the verifier flagged absent,

Reaper arm 4 — failed tenant migrations (reaper.rs):

- New arm between interrupted deletions and self-reservations, using the
  plan's predicate verbatim: status='active' rows with
  migration_failed_at IS NOT NULL whose migration_retry_after has passed
  (or was never set) — fleet_migration::list_retryable_failures. No
  version filter, deliberately: a row whose stamp raced current but
  whose failure state stuck is healed by the no-op retry, where a filter
  would strand it.
- Each due row is retried under the per-account advisory lock (with an
  under-lock re-check) through the boot fleet runner's own per-tenant
  step — fleet_migration::migrate_tenant, now pub(crate) — so a reaper
  retry and a boot attempt run and record identically. Racing a booting
  pod stays safe via atomic-core's per-database migration lock plus the
  monotone GREATEST stamping.
- Per-pass retry cap (ReaperPolicy::max_migration_retries_per_pass,
  default 8) with deferral, mirroring the resume cap and its charging
  rule (settled rows are free). Rows whose count climbs past
  migration_alert_retries (the plan's 5) are escalated at error level
  and surfaced in ReaperSummary::migration_alerts.
- ReaperPolicy::migration_retry embeds the boot runner's
  FleetMigrationConfig; serve hands the reaper loop its --fleet-* config
  so both writers of migration_retry_after share one backoff schedule.
- PG-gated tests (tests/reaper.rs): a due row on a real empty tenant
  database is migrated for real (schema_version verified in-tenant) and
  its failure state cleared, while an unattempted lagging row (the boot
  runner's business) and an inside-horizon row stay untouched; an
  honestly broken row (nonexistent database) re-records a doubled
  horizon, bumps to count 6 and alerts, the cap defers the surplus row,
  and the immediate next pass honors the fresh horizon; contended-lock
  skip + recovery after release.

Additive-only migration lint (tests/migration_lint.rs, un-gated):

- Scans both migration dirs this binary applies — atomic-cloud's
  control-plane migrations and (via path) atomic-core's tenant
  migrations. Forbids exactly the forms that break a still-running old
  binary: DROP TABLE, DROP COLUMN, ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE / SET DATA
  TYPE, and RENAME. DROP INDEX / DROP CONSTRAINT / DROP TRIGGER stay
  allowed: relaxations and the idempotent re-create idiom change no name
  any binary's SQL addresses.
- Comment-aware masking (line + nested block comments, string literals
  with '' escapes, quoted identifiers, dollar-quoted bodies) so a
  forbidden phrase in prose or a plpgsql body never false-positives;
  token-based matching so identifiers like drop_table_marker never do
  either.
- EXEMPT waiver list for the plan's N+1 drops, kept honest both ways: an
  entry must name a file that exists AND still violates, so the list
  can't rot. One entry: core 020 (REAL → DOUBLE PRECISION), which
  predates the additive-only decision and is applied history.
- Fixture probes pin every forbidden form (including the verbatim 020
  text), every allowed relaxation, every masking rule, and the
  line/snippet reporting; a planted-violation run was verified to fail
  with the file, line, and offending statement named.

rather than acknowledges sight-unseen; retry once the run settles), and

signing secret were taken with `#[arg(long, env = …, hide_env_values = true)]`,

Three fixes surfaced verifying slice 8's backup phase:

1. oauth_store: stamp expires_at server-side. insert_oauth_code computed
   expires_at = Utc::now() + ttl on the *client* clock while consume_oauth_code
   filters expires_at > NOW() on the *Postgres server* clock. With a zero TTL,
   any skew where the server's NOW() lagged the client's Utc::now() let a code
   born "expired" still read as live, so expired_code_is_not_consumable_and_purges
   failed deterministically in this environment. The expiry check must be
   evaluated against one clock authority — the server's, since that is where
   consumption is decided. Now insert stamps NOW() + make_interval(secs => $n),
   anchoring both ends (and created_at, already DEFAULT NOW()) to the server
   clock and removing the race. This is a real correctness fix, not a test
   tweak: the test was right to demand a zero-TTL code be inert. No assertion
   was weakened.

2. backup tests: add failed_final_dump_aborts_delete_before_dropping, the
   negative fail-closed path. A FailingPutStore makes the final-dump upload
   fail; the test asserts delete_account errors (BackupStore) and drops
   nothing — the tenant database still exists and its account_databases row
   survives, so the deletion is fully retryable. With hard-delete v1 the final
   dump is the operator's only undo, so this load-bearing guarantee is now
   regression-proof rather than holding only by inspection. A clean retry with
   a working store then drops the DB so the suite leaves nothing behind.

3. main.rs: document why run_backup_loop uses tokio::spawn while the sibling
   reaper uses select! — the backup pass never calls provision_account, so it
   is free of the sqlx higher-ranked-lifetime future that trips spawn's Send

Fixes the adversarial-review findings on slice 8 (backups & DR). All changes
are confined to atomic-cloud; atomic-core and atomic-server are untouched.

1 (timeouts): pg_dump/pg_restore now spawn + are killed on a per-subprocess
  wall-clock budget (--backup-timeout-secs, default 30m) so a hung child can't
  wedge the serial nightly pass forever. A timed-out tenant is killed and
  recorded a typed failure; the pass continues. Whole-pass worst case is bounded
  by timeout × cap (documented).

2 (lock invariant): the HTTP route and CLI delete paths now take the SAME
  per-account advisory lock the nightly pass takes (DeleteLock::Acquire, brief
  retry → CloudError::Busy → 503), so a backup mid-pg_dump and a DROP DATABASE
  of the same tenant are genuinely mutually exclusive. The reaper's
  interrupted-deletion arm already holds the lock, so it passes
  DeleteLock::AlreadyHeld and delete_account skips re-acquisition (no
  self-deadlock). reaper.rs doc comment corrected.

3 (fail-open store): delete_account takes an explicit BackupPolicy
  (Required(store) | DisabledAcknowledged) instead of Option<store>; TenantPlane
  holds Enabled(store) vs DisabledAcknowledged. A forgotten store on an enabled
  path is now a type error, not a silent unrecoverable drop.

4 (cap/deferral): tested — a small cap dumps exactly cap, defers the rest, and
  the next pass reaches the deferred (most-overdue-first).

5 (starvation): ordering is now by last *attempt* (last_backup_attempt_at,
  stamped on success AND failure) so a persistently-failing tenant no longer
  pre-empts a healthy-but-due one every capped pass.

6 (abandoned runs): finalize_abandoned_backup_runs marks stale in-flight

atomic-core: sampling preferences must never constrain strict routing

Live failure on the first cloud tenant: tag extraction on the managed
tagging model (openai/gpt-5-nano) 404'd with OpenRouter's "no endpoints can
handle the requested parameters". Structured calls send
provider.require_parameters=true (the structured-output guarantee) — and
when model capabilities aren't loaded, is_param_supported() fails open and
assumes temperature is universal. The GPT-5 reasoning family rejects
temperature, so the strict filter emptied the endpoint pool: the 404 wasn't
"model missing", it was our own optional preference vetoing every endpoint.

New GenerationParams::is_param_known_supported() returns true only for
positively-loaded capabilities; the OpenRouter completion path uses it for
temperature/max_tokens whenever require_parameters rides. Non-strict
requests keep the permissive fallback (over-sent params are ignored there),
and the streaming path (never strict) is untouched.

web: stamp the build sha into index.html so the PWA shell revision moves

Kenny hit the account-page redirect loop AGAIN a day after the /index.html
fix: workbox carries same-revision precache entries across service-worker
updates WITHOUT refetching, and index.html's bytes (hence its revision)
didn't change between builds — so a client whose cache held the misserved
dashboard document kept serving it after the fixed deploy. The denylist
protected /account routes, but `/` itself still resolved to the poisoned
cached shell.

and therefore its precache revision — unique per deploy, so every SW update
refetches the shell from the (now marker-correct) server. Resolution order:

so cloud.dockerfile takes BUILD_SHA as a build arg, wired from deploy.sh
--build (the droplet clone's HEAD) and cloud-image.yml (github.sha).

cors: let the store-build web clipper reach cloud (and any) servers

A cloud user's extension failed every connection with "Failed to
fetch". Two causes, layered:

The Chrome Web Store build ships activeTab-only (no host_permissions),
so its fetches are ordinary CORS-governed requests — and atomic-cloud
had no CORS middleware at all: the browser's preflight OPTIONS (which
carries no Authorization, per spec) fell through to CloudAuth and died
as a 401 with no Access-Control headers. Unpacked repo installs carry
host_permissions https://*/* which bypasses CORS entirely — which is
why the failure never reproduced for a dev install. The self-hosted
policy had the same gap: is_local_origin never allowed
chrome-extension:// origins.

atomic_server::cors (cloud-unaware generality; both deployments now
share one policy) and allow browser-extension page origins
(chrome-extension://, moz-extension://, safari-web-extension://).
Extensions authenticate with Bearer tokens; supports_credentials stays
off, so cookie-credentialed cross-origin reads remain blocked and the
session-cookie plane keeps its same-origin posture. The cloud wraps the
same policy at its app edge — preflights are answered before CloudAuth.
New e2e pins the contract: extension preflight unauthenticated → 200 +
ACAO, no ACAC; foreign web origin → no CORS headers.

Separately, the user's first logged error was a scheme-less server URL
("you.atomicapp.ai") fetched as a RELATIVE url against the options page
(chrome-extension://…/options/you.atomicapp.ai/api/… →
ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND). The extension now normalizes: https:// prepended
when no scheme is typed (http:// for localhost), applied in the options
form and healing previously-saved configs in getConfig.

atomic-cloud: dispatcher scans no longer pin the AccountCache

Scaling doc #2. Dispatch-path cache reads are non-renewing (get_for_dispatch
never bumps the serving idle TTL), entries built BY a dispatch miss start as
background faults on their own short TTL (background_idle_ttl, 60s, sweep

evidence of non-idleness: a poll finding live ledger state, or a claim that
actually executed (touch on settle). The hard-cap pass evicts by idle
deadline, so scan artifacts are sacrificed before serving entries. Net: a
full scan's residency is a ~60s pulse per 900s interval instead of a
permanent floor, the slow_scan_interval/idle_ttl knobs need no ordering, and
deferred-work tenants (provider backoff, exponential retry) ride one entry
instead of an evict/refault cycle per TTL. slow_scan_interval default
300s -> 900s (the lost-hint recovery bound / cron pickup floor, documented).

only) churned deferred-work tenants, and the reviewers proved the
900s == 900s zero-margin interaction between scan interval and idle TTL;
the background-TTL layer answers both. Five new tests pin the invariants at
the cache layer and through real dispatcher ticks.

tests: fix parallel-execution flake in deferred_pipeline_leaves_jobs_in_ledger

The test drained the parked job through process_queued_pipeline_jobs and
asserted the returned admitted-count was 1. That path routes through the
process-global EMBEDDING_BATCH_SEMAPHORE (2 permits, shared across every
database — and therefore across every concurrently running test in the
binary). When siblings hold both permits, the saturated branch parks an
empty-handed waiter and returns 0 by design; the job is still processed
moments later. The assertion was therefore sensitive to sibling-test
contention: reliably green in isolation or with --test-threads=1, near-
deterministically red on a loaded machine, intermittently red on CI
(first seen on main Jul 19, twice more on PR #223's runs).

Drain through run_pipeline_jobs_batch instead — the deferred-mode worker
entry point, which claims synchronously and takes no semaphore — so the
claimed-count assertion holds regardless of what the rest of the binary
is doing. This also matches the production topology the test simulates:
hosts that turn inline execution off drive the ledger from a worker, not
from the fire-and-forget spawn path.

Product code is unchanged; the saturated-path behavior it asserts around
is working as designed.

tests: await_pipeline tolerates a run claimed by another worker

update_lifecycle_sqlite failed on main (Jul 26) with "event channel closed
before pipeline finished". A save's on_event sink is not guaranteed to
observe that save's own pipeline run: the job ledger is per-storage but
workers are spawned per-call and drain the ledger before releasing their
permit, so a still-draining worker from an earlier save can claim this
atom's job and emit into that earlier call's sink. The originating call
then claims an empty queue, takes the fast path's early return without
spawning, and drops the only sender its channel had.

Product code is correct as written. Every production sink is process-wide
(atomic-server's broadcast channel, Tauri's app_handle.emit), so the events
reach clients regardless of which call's callback carried them. Only a
per-call test channel can observe the difference, and it sees it as a
closed channel.

So await_pipeline falls back to the durable atom record when its channel
closes. That is a stronger assertion than the event stream, not a weaker
one: it verifies the work actually landed rather than that one particular
callback saw it happen.

The interleaving is too narrow to reproduce by stress (80 runs under 10x
CPU oversubscription, zero hits), so a new test stages it deterministically
instead — the saving call gets no worker at all (deferred mode) and an
unrelated sink drains the job. It reproduces the original panic exactly
without this fix.

fix: a padded 200 is a truncated transfer, not a parse failure

A gateway fronting a slow upstream commits `200 OK` before the work is
done, then holds the connection open with insignificant JSON whitespace
(OpenRouter writes a newline-and-spaces heartbeat every ~425ms, legal
because RFC 8259 allows whitespace before the top-level value). Once the
status is committed it cannot be retracted, so a late failure can only
be an error body or an ended stream. When the stream ends, the client
gets a complete, well-formed 200 whose entire body is padding.

We classified that as a permanent ParseError. Auto-tagging therefore
spent one attempt of a three-attempt budget and dropped the atom — on a
fault a retry fixes, and one OpenRouter records as a success and bills
for. The identical event cut a moment earlier arrived as Network and was
retried; only the politely-terminated form was fatal.

serde_json draws the line: Category::Eof means the input ran out (empty,
all padding, or cut mid-JSON) and is always a truncated transfer, while
Syntax/Data mean bytes arrived and were wrong. `decode_error` applies it
across both chat and both embedding paths.

Also fixed, same class:

- Both streaming parsers returned Ok with empty content when the stream
  carried no payload at all, persisting the silence as if the model had
  chosen it. Guarded on "no SSE payload and no terminator" so a
  legitimately empty completion is untouched.
- The chat path had no handling for a 200 carrying an error object — the
  gateway's other exit. `choices` is required, so it landed as a
  permanent parse failure. The embedding path's handling is now shared
  via `upstream_error` in openrouter/mod.rs.
- `x-generation-id` arrives in the headers, before the body, so it
  survives exactly the failures the body doesn't. Captured into the
  error and log line; it resolves to provider, timings, finish reason
  and cost via GET /api/v1/generation.
- Response previews were logged raw, so a padded body printed as a blank
  field — the diagnostic went dark precisely when the body mattered.
  `body_for_log` describes whitespace bodies and escapes everything else.
- Tagging sent no max_tokens at all: StructuredCall::new sets a default
  and with_params replaced the struct wholesale. That changes routing —
  OpenRouter filters endpoints by max_completion_tokens. call_structured
  now guarantees a cap, and tagging sets 8192 explicitly (32k prunes
  real endpoints from the pool; 8192 clears the worst observed
  generation, 3091 tokens, with room to spare).

padding is present on every non-streaming call, the JSON payload has
zero newlines (so `line 233` in the report was 232 padding newlines),
and the measured 4.66 newlines/sec cadence independently reproduces the

bytes and the real chunked framing.

fix: take tag extraction off wire-level structured output

`response_format` puts the endpoint's constrained-decoding implementation
in the path, and implementations vary. Measured on
`google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` via OpenRouter, DeepInfra's schema-enforced
endpoint returned a valid-but-empty `{"tags": []}` on roughly one call in
three — 8 completion tokens, finish_reason stop, zero reasoning tokens,
no error signal anywhere — and schema-mode tag counts swung 5 to 13 on
identical input. The decoder took the shortest grammar-valid path instead
of doing the task.

Empty-but-valid is the worst failure shape available. It parses, so
`call_structured`'s prompt-based fallback never fires, and it reaches the
pipeline looking like an answer: the atom is recorded tagged with
nothing, `tagging_status = complete`, and never reconsidered.

Tag extraction is generative — the model decides how many tags to emit —
so a decoder that shortens the output changes the answer, not just its
shape. Schema now goes in the prompt for that call, parsed tolerantly.

The trade is a decoding guarantee for the tolerant parser, and the parser
was measured never to be exercised: across openai/gpt-5-nano,
google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, openai/gpt-5-mini and z-ai/glm-5.2, all 24
prompt-mode replies parsed directly — no fences, no surrounding prose.
Prompt mode also matched or beat schema mode on tag count for three of
the four models and was consistently less erratic.

`SchemaEnforcement` makes the choice explicit rather than implied by a
bool: Strict and Lenient both send `response_format`, PromptOnly sends
none. `with_strict` remains as shorthand over the two wire-level modes,
so it can never silently reach a different transport. Only tag extraction
moves; tag consolidation stays on constrained decoding because the
degradation was not measured for its prompt and output shape.

This also corrects the claim in `call_long_form_markdown`'s docs that
short structured calls "genuinely benefit from constrained decoding" —
true of shaping, not of generating.

The mock AI server routes schema-less requests by sniffing the schema
stated in the prompt; extraction and consolidation both carry
`parent_name`, so consolidation is tested first.

empty one.
